name: file
description: Determines the type of a file by examining its magic numbers and content, not just its extension.

flags.description: Brief mode: omit the filename prefix.

examples.output: photo: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, ... 1920x1080
examples.explanation: Reveals that "photo" (no extension) is actually a JPEG image.
Prints the MIME type and detected character encoding.

examples.output: backup.tar.gz: gzip compressed data, original size 52428800
examples.explanation: Identifies the compression format regardless of the filename.

about: file reads the beginning of a file and compares it against a database of magic signatures (/usr/share/misc/magic). This is how it detects executables, images, archives, and text encodings without relying on filenames.
useCases: Identify files with missing or wrong extensions.
Verify that a download is really the expected format.
Check text encodings before processing files with scripts.
mistakes: Trusting extensions: a file named data.csv may actually be a zip archive; file tells the truth.
